claims.statement: MHFC is a fictional Delaware-incorporated financial holding company headquartered in Charlotte Bay, NC, operating in 31 countries, organized into three reportable segments (CCB, CIB, AWM) plus a Corporate segment comprising Treasury/CIO and Other Corporate.
In January 2025 the corporate and investment banking business was combined with Commercial Banking into a single Commercial & Investment Bank, with integration completed in 2025.

2025 segment results: CCB net revenue $40,800mm/net income $12,300mm (ROE 30%), CIB $32,450mm/$10,180mm (18%), AWM $13,180mm/$3,580mm (32%), Corporate $(330)mm/$(1,100)mm, totaling $86,100mm revenue and $24,960mm net income; segment capital is allocated from standalone risk profile including SCB and G-SIB surcharge.

Consolidated 2025 results: net income $24,960mm, diluted EPS $16.93, ROTCE 26.4%, overhead ratio 54.9%, Standardized CET1 15.1%, total assets $1,418,560mm, loans $742,300mm, deposits $1,012,400mm, headcount 214,600.

Q2 2026: net income $6.54bn, EPS $4.48, revenue $22.48bn up 5.4% YoY, CET1 15.1%, $4.6bn returned to shareholders; segment net income CCB 3,210, CIB 2,740, AWM 960, Corporate (370); 2026 NII outlook raised from about $50.2bn to about $50.5bn with adjusted expense about $49.5bn and Card NCO rate about 3.6%.

Risk governance follows three lines of defense; the CRO (Dana K. Whitfield) reports to the CEO and Board Risk Committee, MRGR reports to the CRO, and named management committees (Firmwide Risk, ALCO, Capital Governance chaired by the CFO, Allowance, Firmwide Model Risk, Data and Technology Risk) own oversight of rates, capital, allowance, models and data/API change management.

The Board-approved risk appetite sets limits including Standardized CET1 >= 13.0% baseline, stressed CET1 >= 10.2%, SLR >= 5.5%, LCR >= 110%, NII decline under -200bp <= 7.0%, Card NCO <= 4.5%; all were within limit at December 31, 2025.

The binding capital ratio is Standardized CET1 (the lower of Standardized and Advanced under the Collins Floor); the 10.2% requirement is 4.5% minimum + 3.2% SCB (effective Oct 1, 2025 to Sep 30, 2026) + 2.5% G-SIB surcharge with 0% CCyB, against a management target of about 13.0%; the Firm expects SCB to remain 3.2% from Oct 1, 2026 based on preliminary results received June 27, 2026.

2025 capital actions: $4.30/share dividends ($6.1bn), $11.0bn repurchases (38.3mm shares), and a new $30bn repurchase program approved June 2025 through 2028; the Q2 2026 capital plan assumes $3.0bn per quarter of buybacks and $1.15 quarterly dividends, with management cautious about deploying excess capital pending final rules and confirmation of SCB in August.

Treasury/CIO owns liquidity risk management with independent oversight from Liquidity Risk Oversight in the Chief Risk Office; average Q4 2025 LCR was 116% and NSFR 128%, and average 2Q26 LCR was 115%.

MHFC discloses through three reports: the 2025 Annual Report (Feb 2026), the Pillar 3 disclosures (March 2026, covering the consolidated bank holding company, unaudited but subject to Disclosure Committee review and consistent with FR Y-9C, FFIEC 101 and FR Y-15), and the Q2 2026 earnings supplement (July 14, 2026) whose capital ratios are estimates finalized in the FR Y-9C prepared from API-16 data.

Quarterly-refreshed model outputs such as capital projections are intentionally omitted from the annual and Pillar 3 reports and published in the quarterly earnings materials, while year-end allowance by segment and scenario-weight sensitivity are in the Annual Report's Note 6 and referenced by the Q2 2026 supplement.

MHFC owns about 2,900 models under a Model Risk Policy aligned with SR 11-7; Tier 1 models need annual independent MRGR validation, quarterly monitoring, annual owner attestation and Firmwide Model Risk Committee approval; three Tier 1 models (MDL-ALM-014, MDL-CR-007, MDL-CAP-003) directly drive disclosed figures, with distinct owners, upstream APIs and validation dates.

Reported 2025 MRGR findings: MDL-CR-007 had a medium finding on unfunded commitments (interim overlay) and a low finding on Card PD elasticity documentation; MDL-ALM-014 had a medium finding on constant deposit betas mitigated by quarterly dynamic simulation; MDL-CAP-003 had nothing above low severity.

MHFC operates one Developer Platform exposing eighteen production APIs with OAuth 2.0 (mutual TLS server-to-server), rate limiting and SLO monitoring; the same governed APIs serve clients and feed risk models and regulatory reports, with six classified as critical data services (Credit Risk Scoring, Loan Servicing, Market Data, Macroeconomic Scenario, Treasury Liquidity Positions, Regulatory Reporting).
Platform usage rose from an average 4.0bn calls/month at 99.97% availability in 2025 to 4.4bn calls/month at 99.98% in 2Q26.

A breaking change to an upstream API's schema or business logic automatically opens a model change review because upstream APIs are registered critical data sources in the model inventory; data-quality exceptions on critical data elements are reported monthly to the Data and Technology Risk Committee, and API-16 outputs are automatically reconciled to the general ledger by legal entity.
Migrating the Macroeconomic Scenario API to the strategic data platform cut scenario-load time for the CECL and capital models from six hours to under forty minutes.

The capital model is re-run quarterly over a nine-quarter horizon; under stress buybacks are suspended and dividends held flat, and the indicative SCB equals peak-to-trough CET1 decline plus four quarters of dividends over starting RWA, floored at 2.5% (Q2 2026 indicative SCB 3.18% vs preliminary 3.2%).

NII sensitivity is measured on a static balance sheet with instantaneous parallel shocks and constant deposit betas (0.45 consumer, 0.75 wholesale); at year-end 2025 the Firm was asset-sensitive (+100bp adds $1,508mm, -200bp removes $3,017mm or 6.0%, within the 7.0% limit), with non-parallel moves and management actions captured only in the quarterly dynamic simulation.

The allowance was $15,920mm (2.14% of loans) at Dec 31, 2025 and $16,380mm (2.15%) at June 30, 2026, produced by MDL-CR-007 with scenario weights Upside 20%/Baseline 50%/Downside 30% approved by the Allowance Committee; a 100% downside weighting would raise it by about $4.2bn.

At year-end 2025 the Standardized capital conservation buffer was 10.58% versus 5.7% required, so there were no distribution limits; Meridian Harbor Bank, N.A. is the principal insured depository institution and is separately well capitalized, with no impediments to intra-Firm capital transfers beyond those generally applicable to U.S. bank holding companies.
